questions.question: Dr. Ayoub took a periapical radiograph that appears too light. Dr. Nadia asks him to check his settings. Which parameter is likely involved?
questions.explanation: Dr. Nadia explains: 'Too low mA produces fewer photons, making the image underexposed and therefore too light.' Dr. Ayoub: 'I will increase the mA.'

questions.question: Dr. Nadia examines a radiograph with very low contrast. Dr. Ayoub asks her which setting could improve contrast. Dr. Nadia replies:
questions.explanation: Dr. Nadia explains: 'A lower kV produces higher contrast (more contrasted image).' Dr. Ayoub: 'I will lower the kV to 60-65.'

questions.question: Dr. Ayoub performed a panoramic on a patient with jewelry. Dr. Nadia shows him a linear white artifact. What is the cause of this artifact?
options: The presence of a metal jewel (earring, piercing)
A defect in the panoramic sensor
questions.explanation: Dr. Nadia explains: 'Metal jewelry creates radiation artifacts (white lines or dark bands) on panoramics.' Dr. Ayoub: 'I will always ask to remove jewelry.'

questions.question: Dr. Nadia shows a periapical radiograph with an elongated image. Dr. Ayoub asks: 'What technical error was made?' Dr. Nadia replies:
options: A vertical angulation that is too positive
A vertical angulation that is too negative
A focal-film distance that is too long
questions.explanation: Dr. Nadia explains: 'A vertical angulation that is too positive (too open) elongates the tooth (image longer than reality).' Dr. Ayoub: 'I will correct my angulation.'

questions.question: Dr. Ayoub notices that the image is shortened on a periapical radiograph. Dr. Nadia asks him to check his angulation. What is the likely error?
options: A vertical angulation that is too positive
A vertical angulation that is too negative
A horizontal angulation that is too large
A focal-film distance that is too short
questions.explanation: Dr. Nadia explains: 'A vertical angulation that is too negative (too closed) shortens the image.' Dr. Ayoub: 'I will adjust my angle.'

questions.question: Dr. Nadia explains to Dr. Ayoub the phenomenon of the anode effect (Heel effect). She asks him to correctly position the cathode. Where should the cathode be oriented?
options: Towards the top of the skull
questions.explanation: Dr. Nadia explains: 'The anode effect makes the beam more intense on the cathode side. For molars, orient the cathode towards the bone thickness.' Dr. Ayoub: 'I will position it correctly.'

questions.question: Dr. Ayoub took a Bitewing radiograph on a patient. Dr. Nadia asks him to check if the interproximal spaces are well visible. What is the key setting for a quality Bitewing?
options: A vertical angulation of +5 to +10 degrees
questions.explanation: Dr. Nadia explains: 'A slight positive angulation (+5 to +10°) opens the interproximal spaces.' Dr. Ayoub: 'I will always use this angulation.'

questions.question: Dr. Nadia shows a radiograph where the maxillary sinus is poorly visualized. Dr. Ayoub asks: 'Which view would allow better visualization of the sinuses?'
questions.explanation: Dr. Nadia explains: 'The Blondeau view clears the maxillary sinuses by projecting the petrous ridges below the sinus floor.' Dr. Ayoub: 'I will use this view.'

questions.question: Dr. Ayoub took a radiograph of an implant. Dr. Nadia asks him to check the image quality. What parameter is crucial for evaluating osseointegration?
options: High spatial resolution to see the bone-implant interface
High contrast to see soft tissues
questions.explanation: Dr. Nadia explains: 'High spatial resolution is essential to evaluate the bone-implant interface.' Dr. Ayoub: 'I will use the smallest possible pixel size.'

questions.question: Dr. Nadia explains to Dr. Ayoub the importance of the collimator. Dr. Ayoub asks: 'What is the collimator used for in dental radiology?'
options: To reduce secondary scattering and limit the exposure field
questions.explanation: Dr. Nadia explains: 'The collimator limits the exposure field, reduces scattering, and protects adjacent tissues.' Dr. Ayoub: 'I will always use the collimator.'

questions.question: Dr. Ayoub notices an opaque area on a panoramic radiograph. Dr. Nadia asks him to identify the structure. It is most likely:
options: The cervical spine projected onto the mandibular ramus
questions.explanation: Dr. Nadia explains: 'On a panoramic, the cervical spine can project onto the mandibular ramus, creating an opaque area (cervical shadow).' Dr. Ayoub: 'I will learn to recognize this projection.'

questions.question: Dr. Nadia shows a radiograph of an interproximal cavity. Dr. Ayoub asks: 'Which view allows detection of interproximal cavities?'
questions.explanation: Dr. Nadia explains: 'The Bitewing is the reference examination for interproximal cavities.' Dr. Ayoub: 'I will systematically prescribe Bitewings.'

questions.question: Dr. Ayoub took a radiograph of a pregnant patient. Dr. Nadia reminds him of the radiation protection rules. What is the absolute rule?
options: Never perform radiographic examinations during pregnancy
Perform only if justified and with absolute protection
Limit the examination to CBCT only
Increase the dose to reduce exposure time
questions.explanation: Dr. Nadia explains: 'We perform an X-ray only if strictly justified, with a lead apron and by limiting the area.' Dr. Ayoub: 'I will always justify my examinations.'

questions.question: Dr. Nadia explains to Dr. Ayoub the principle of the bisecting angle technique. Dr. Ayoub asks: 'When is this technique used?'
questions.explanation: Dr. Nadia explains: 'The bisecting angle technique is used when anatomy does not allow paralleling (e.g., deep palate).' Dr. Ayoub: 'I will use it when needed.'

questions.question: Dr. Ayoub took a radiograph of the TMJ. Dr. Nadia asks him which view is most suitable. Dr. Nadia replies:
questions.explanation: Dr. Nadia explains: 'The Schüller view is classic for visualizing the TMJ.' Dr. Ayoub: 'I will use this view.'

questions.question: Dr. Nadia shows a radiograph with a kinetic blur effect. Dr. Ayoub asks: 'How to avoid kinetic blur?'
options: Decrease exposure time and immobilize the patient
questions.explanation: Dr. Nadia explains: 'A short time and strict immobilization avoid motion blur.' Dr. Ayoub: 'I will use a very short time.'

questions.question: Dr. Ayoub took a radiograph of a child. Dr. Nadia asks him to adapt the parameters. What modification should be made?
options: Decrease kV and mA to reduce dose
Use the same parameters as for an adult
questions.explanation: Dr. Nadia explains: 'Children have lower bone density. We reduce parameters (kV, mA, time).' Dr. Ayoub: 'I will always adapt the parameters.'

questions.question: Dr. Nadia shows a radiograph with a periapical radiolucent area. Dr. Ayoub asks: 'What is the most probable differential diagnosis?'
questions.explanation: Dr. Nadia explains: 'A periapical radiolucent area suggests a periapical pathology.' Dr. Ayoub: 'I will prescribe endodontic treatment.'

questions.question: Dr. Ayoub performed a CBCT on a patient. Dr. Nadia asks him to check the field of view (FOV). Why should the FOV be limited?
questions.explanation: Dr. Nadia explains: 'A small FOV reduces dose, improves resolution, and accelerates acquisition.' Dr. Ayoub: 'I will always use the smallest possible FOV.'

questions.question: Dr. Nadia explains to Dr. Ayoub the radiographic signs of periodontitis. Dr. Ayoub asks: 'What is the characteristic radiographic sign of periodontitis?'
options: Loss of alveolar bone (horizontal or vertical bone pattern)
questions.explanation: Dr. Nadia explains: 'Periodontitis is characterized by alveolar bone loss (horizontal or vertical).' Dr. Ayoub: 'I will evaluate the alveolar bone.'

questions.question: Dr. Ayoub took a radiograph of a tooth with internal resorption. Dr. Nadia asks him to describe the image. How does internal resorption appear?
options: A symmetrical radiolucent area centered on the canal
questions.explanation: Dr. Nadia explains: 'Internal resorption is a symmetrical radiolucent area that follows the contour of the canal.' Dr. Ayoub: 'I will monitor the evolution.'

questions.question: Dr. Nadia shows a radiograph of a tooth with a root fracture. Dr. Ayoub asks: 'What is the radiographic sign of a root fracture?'
options: A vertical radiolucent line crossing the root
questions.explanation: Dr. Nadia explains: 'A root fracture appears as a vertical radiolucent line.' Dr. Ayoub: 'I will orient the beam perpendicularly.'

questions.question: Dr. Ayoub wonders about the difference between a granuloma and an apical cyst. Dr. Nadia replies: 'The difference is based on:'
options: The size of the lesion (cyst > granuloma)
questions.explanation: Dr. Nadia explains: 'A cyst is generally larger than a granuloma (> 1.5-2 cm).' Dr. Ayoub: 'I will measure the lesion.'

questions.question: Dr. Nadia shows a radiograph of a patient with an impacted tooth. Dr. Ayoub asks: 'What is the most frequent location of impacted teeth?'
questions.explanation: Dr. Nadia explains: 'Mandibular wisdom teeth are the most frequently impacted teeth.' Dr. Ayoub: 'I will always check the wisdom teeth.'

questions.question: Dr. Ayoub, after having mastered radiological techniques with Dr. Nadia, receives her congratulations. What is the next step for Dr. Ayoub?
options: Become an expert in radiology and dental imaging
questions.explanation: Dr. Nadia explains: 'Mastery of radiology is a valuable skill. Becoming an expert is the next step.' Dr. Ayoub: 'I will deepen 3D imaging.'
